When I was much younger, before I even knew who Warren Buffett was, I enjoyed growing things in dirt. Warren Buffett always says that he prefers to own a farm over owning something like gold. A farm produces something creating things out of nothing, where as gold sits there doing nothing. While I now do it on a much larger scale and deal with people who do it on an even larger scale, I want to help people understand the importance of true value over currency value and how the act of just growing vegetables in your garden is in itself, a business.

First, the most important commodity in the world is food. Every one needs it and just look at the countries that don't have it. What is the first thing people start stealing when their economy collapses? Look at Venezuela. A lot of people have always said that you can't eat money. So what happens when farms corporate themselves into money making machines? Say all western economies collapsed today. All industrial farms would stop and they would not being able to provide. Traditional farms and backyard farms would survive. People who earn hundreds of thousands of dollars, now earn hundreds and thousands of nothing. These people, with no spending power, would revert back to farmers or serfs. In these times, you can hold a potato next to $100 and choose a potato. Any persons instinct will drive them to gain food in times of need.

As prices of everything go up, how does the value of food change? It doesn't. The same amount of food still provides sustenance for the same amount of people, no matter how much it costs. So what happens when food costs nothing? No matter where I have lived, I have always grown my own food to at least supplement my own meals, even if I am fully capable of buying everything. (Its usually healthier and tastier too to grow your own food).

Right now, if there is an emergency and the economy collapses or food becomes scarce, I can live off my property. I will admit though, that my land is a bit bigger than most peoples, but you can grow a lot of food in a very small place. Even on apartment balconies. The internet can tell you how.

So how does growing your own food relate to running a business? A business is the act of doing something that produces something for someone else, in order to gain something back in return. Usually, it is produce something, serve someone, get money rewards. Now, you might be an employee of business you do not own, but the fact is, that business is paying you to serve them, so its really the same. Your business, is your time. Now, one of the first things most people would do with their money is ensure they have enough to buy some food. So, you are giving your time, to someone/something else, in exchange for food. The same principle can be applied to your garden. You can give your time, to grow your own food and in turn get "money" in the form of food, as payment for services rendered to your garden). Which is now something you do not have to spend on your money on.

Summary:

As money becomes worthless, food's true value does not change. Its value that you measure in money will change, but it doesn't change its true value. Make the most of the situation now while you can set up a garden.

Growing your own food is no different than working for something else to make money and buy food. Every one should do it.
